observations.finding: vs DMSO spread diffuse green filamentous tubulin, treated cells at 5uM (f_1dbcaa471451, f_13b3d82aad0a) show markedly brighter green/yellow tubulin signal with coarse, punctate/bundled texture and high local contrast; effect stronger at 15uM (f_ce9400223061, f_53e85790df0c) with intensely yellow co-stained rounded cells and spindle-like cells with long thin projections on black background. vs DMSO red cortical actin rim, treated fields show increased red puncta at cell periphery and increased yellow overlap with tubulin, with heterogeneous patchy intensity and higher texture contrast, most evident in bright round cells at 15uM.

vs DMSO large polygonal spread cells, treated cells are compact, reduced in overall cell area/length, rounded or teardrop-shaped with narrow projections; clusters of very bright yellow round cells suggest mitotic condensation.

vs DMSO oval blue nuclei of uniform size, treated nuclei appear smaller, more condensed and darker/irregular, with reduced long axis; many bright round yellow cells have condensed DNA co-localized with tubulin/actin consistent with mitotic cells. Visible reduction in nuclear size.

cell number/density visibly lower in treated fields vs DMSO control of same plate: 5uM fields show large empty black areas and ~moderate density; 15uM fields are very sparse with only 10-20 cells per 1024x819 px field and vast empty area (f_53e85790df0c ~ <10 cells). Quantitative cell counts: 288 cells measured at 5uM vs 69 at 15uM indicating dose-dependent loss. No cell-count/density feature is listed in top_deviations, so observation is not covered by provided measurements.

data.note:
Noted - unblinding shows error: Actin disruptors (0.55) vs true BBBC021 class Cholesterol-lowering for mevinolin/lovastatin.

PubChem CID 53232 confirms lovastatin/mevinolin identity; ChEMBL CHEMBL503 annotates HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor mechanism.

Literature explains the phenotypic mimicry: the canonical mechanism is HMG CoA reductase inhibition (PMID 3076125). At high dose (5-15 µM) this produced extreme actin/tubulin texture increases (z up to +66) and cell shrinkage that quantitatively resembled actin disruptors in the reference atlas (Actin 4/10 neighbours, NSC 2/4). However statins are known to alter cytoskeleton organization and inhibit experimental metastasis via cytoskeletal changes (PMID 12405293) and modulate the Rho/actin/cell rigidity pathway (PMID 26451103) via impaired isoprenylation downstream of mevalonate, producing secondary actin-like rounding/bundling. This accounts for why the highest-dose profile was dominated by act/tub contrast rather than a cholesterol-lowering signature, which in the atlas was only represented by a single simvastatin neighbour at similarity 0.77. The requested 1.5 µM onset well could not be acquired due to exhausted budget (0/4 left), preventing discrimination of actin-led vs tubulin-led onset.

Lesson: for pleiotropic cholesterol-lowering compounds, high-dose cytoskeletal secondary effects can outscore the primary MoA in morphology profiling.

reflection.text:
Unblinded truth: mevinolin/lovastatin, Cholesterol-lowering (HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor), agent predicted Actin disruptors p=0.62 then 0.55 - verdict incorrect. This reflection is scored post-unblinding against the evidence actually acquired in this run.

What the evidence got right: At 5uM and 15uM there was an extreme high-contrast texture phenotype: tub_glcm_contrast z=+24.8 to +66.8 (e2,e4), act_glcm_contrast z=+22.4 to +41.7 (e2,e4), act_std z=+20.5 to +37.0, with steep dose-dependence rho=+0.80 to +1.00 for tub_glcm_contrast, act_glcm_contrast, tub_std, act_std (e7,e11,e17,e18), correlated with cell loss rho=-1.00 cell_count (e9) to 69 cells at 15uM (e4) and cell/nuclear shrinkage rho=-1.00 cell_area, nuc_area (e12,e13). This correctly identified a real morphological stress/on-target downstream effect, but not the primary MOA. The review critique was accurate: both actin and tubulin channels surged together at saturated doses, with act_tub_ratio rho=-1.00 (e19), so discrimination was impossible from those 4 wells alone. Low doses were essentially baseline: 0.15uM frac_multinucleate_proxy +2.8 only (e5), 0.5uM frac_large_nucleus +4.2 (e3), no progressive texture, confirming no early morphology before the 5uM cliff.

What misled and why acquisition/comparison choices mattered: 
1. Reference atlas forced misclassification. compare_to_reference_atlas (e6) voted Actin disruptors 2/4 NSC, k-neighbours Actin 4/10 mean 0.832 vs Microtubule stabilizers 3/10 mean 0.775 vs Protein degradation 1/10. With Cholesterol-lowering not represented as a morphological class in the atlas, the system could only map secondary cytoskeletal changes to the nearest cytoskeleton class. The margin was narrow and based on only 4 acquired wells, two single-replicate high-dose wells at 0.90 similarity - over-interpreted as prior for Actin.
2. Dose placement. list_available_experiments showed 8 doses 0.015-50uM (e1), but we spent the 4-well budget on 0.15, 0.5, 5, 15uM. As the review noted, 0.5uM was still baseline and 5uM already saturated with tubulin +24.8 and actin +22.4, so we never tested the onset dose 1.5uM (dose index 4) that was requested to see which channel moves first. Second-time describe_phenotype on low-dose fields (e16 density higher vs DMSO, unknown) vs high-dose describe_phenotype (e10 density lower, Microtubule stabilizers) highlighted microscopist uncertainty, but we weighted the quantitative atlas over e10's Microtubule stabilizer call.
3. Statistics over-read. e7 and e8 rho=+0.80 p=0.2 with n=4 wells were cited as trends but p=0.2 is not significant; only e9,e11,e12,e13,e17-e19 rho=+/-1.00 p=0 reached significance, all driven by the 5-15uM saturated points. update_hypotheses (e14 Actin 0.59 vs Microtubule 0.33, e20 Actin 0.55 vs 0.38) correctly kept Microtubule stabilizers as runner-up but we still submitted (e15,e21) at p=0.62/0.55 prematurely without the requested 1.5uM well, as flagged in review verdict request_experiment.

Why truth was missed despite lookup: Post-unblinding lookup_compound showed PubChem CID 53232; e22 reported none curated for mevinolin/lovastatin combined, but e24 on lovastatin alone returned HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor, consistent with literature PMID 3076125 on mechanism of HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors. The phenotypic mimicry is explained by downstream biology, not direct actin binding: PMID 12405293 shows lovastatin alters cytoskeleton organization and inhibits metastasis of mammary carcinoma cells, PMID 26451103 shows simvastatin enhances Rho/actin/cell rigidity pathway, PMID 16929252 on geranylgeranylated proteins in proliferation, and PMID 14630613 on cytoskeletal activation and altered gene expression by simvastatin - i.e., statin depletion of isoprenoids impairs Rho-family prenylation, producing secondary actin/tubulin texture, rounding and shrinkage at high micromolar doses that the atlas reads as Actin disruptors. PMID 31687098 and PMID 15571475 similarly discuss lovastatin/statin as cholesterol-lowering agents via HMG-CoA reductase, not direct cytoskeleton targets.

Lesson: With a limited atlas, simultaneous actin+ tubulin surge + cell loss should trigger suspicion of off-target/downstream cytoskeletal effect rather than direct Actin disruptor, and requires onset-dose titration and orthogonal biochemical assays (actin polymerization vs tubulin polymerization, and Rho prenylation readouts) before assigning p>0.6.
what_was_right: Extreme high-dose morphology real (e2,e4) with tub_glcm_contrast up to +66.8, actin contrast +41.7, dose rho 0.8-1.0
Baseline at 0.15-0.5uM e3,e5 vs saturated at 5uM e2 confirmed steep threshold requiring onset dose
Review correctly identified atlas margin 4/10 vs 3/10 e6 insufficient and 0.62 premature
what_was_wrong: Mapped Cholesterol-lowering downstream cytoskeletal effect to direct Actin disruptor due to atlas lacking cholesterol class
Weighted NSC 2/4 and k-neighbour 4/10 over microscopist Microtubule stabilizer call e10
Used n=4 rho p=0.2 e7,e8 as supportive trend and submitted without requested 1.5uM well
reflection.next_experiment: Acquire 1.5uM onset well plus full 0.5-5uM titration with act_* vs tub_* texture and act_tub_ratio trajectory + blinded reference actin and microtubule compounds; add orthogonal assays: in vitro actin polymerization/F-actin sedimentation vs tubulin polymerization counter-assay and Rho geranylgeranylation/prenylation readout to separate HMG-CoA reductase downstream cytoskeleton effect from direct actin disruption.

## Reflection

Unblinded truth: mevinolin/lovastatin, Cholesterol-lowering (HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor), agent predicted Actin disruptors p=0.62 then 0.55 - verdict incorrect. This reflection is scored post-unblinding against the evidence actually acquired in this run.

What the evidence got right: At 5uM and 15uM there was an extreme high-contrast texture phenotype: tub_glcm_contrast z=+24.8 to +66.8 (e2,e4), act_glcm_contrast z=+22.4 to +41.7 (e2,e4), act_std z=+20.5 to +37.0, with steep dose-dependence rho=+0.80 to +1.00 for tub_glcm_contrast, act_glcm_contrast, tub_std, act_std (e7,e11,e17,e18), correlated with cell loss rho=-1.00 cell_count (e9) to 69 cells at 15uM (e4) and cell/nuclear shrinkage rho=-1.00 cell_area, nuc_area (e12,e13). This correctly identified a real morphological stress/on-target downstream effect, but not the primary MOA. The review critique was accurate: both actin and tubulin channels surged together at saturated doses, with act_tub_ratio rho=-1.00 (e19), so discrimination was impossible from those 4 wells alone. Low doses were essentially baseline: 0.15uM frac_multinucleate_proxy +2.8 only (e5), 0.5uM frac_large_nucleus +4.2 (e3), no progressive texture, confirming no early morphology before the 5uM cliff.

What misled and why acquisition/comparison choices mattered: 
1. Reference atlas forced misclassification. compare_to_reference_atlas (e6) voted Actin disruptors 2/4 NSC, k-neighbours Actin 4/10 mean 0.832 vs Microtubule stabilizers 3/10 mean 0.775 vs Protein degradation 1/10. With Cholesterol-lowering not represented as a morphological class in the atlas, the system could only map secondary cytoskeletal changes to the nearest cytoskeleton class. The margin was narrow and based on only 4 acquired wells, two single-replicate high-dose wells at 0.90 similarity - over-interpreted as prior for Actin.
2. Dose placement. list_available_experiments showed 8 doses 0.015-50uM (e1), but we spent the 4-well budget on 0.15, 0.5, 5, 15uM. As the review noted, 0.5uM was still baseline and 5uM already saturated with tubulin +24.8 and actin +22.4, so we never tested the onset dose 1.5uM (dose index 4) that was requested to see which channel moves first. Second-time describe_phenotype on low-dose fields (e16 density higher vs DMSO, unknown) vs high-dose describe_phenotype (e10 density lower, Microtubule stabilizers) highlighted microscopist uncertainty, but we weighted the quantitative atlas over e10's Microtubule stabilizer call.
3. Statistics over-read. e7 and e8 rho=+0.80 p=0.2 with n=4 wells were cited as trends but p=0.2 is not significant; only e9,e11,e12,e13,e17-e19 rho=+/-1.00 p=0 reached significance, all driven by the 5-15uM saturated points. update_hypotheses (e14 Actin 0.59 vs Microtubule 0.33, e20 Actin 0.55 vs 0.38) correctly kept Microtubule stabilizers as runner-up but we still submitted (e15,e21) at p=0.62/0.55 prematurely without the requested 1.5uM well, as flagged in review verdict request_experiment.

Why truth was missed despite lookup: Post-unblinding lookup_compound showed PubChem CID 53232; e22 reported none curated for mevinolin/lovastatin combined, but e24 on lovastatin alone returned HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor, consistent with literature PMID 3076125 on mechanism of HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors. The phenotypic mimicry is explained by downstream biology, not direct actin binding: PMID 12405293 shows lovastatin alters cytoskeleton organization and inhibits metastasis of mammary carcinoma cells, PMID 26451103 shows simvastatin enhances Rho/actin/cell rigidity pathway, PMID 16929252 on geranylgeranylated proteins in proliferation, and PMID 14630613 on cytoskeletal activation and altered gene expression by simvastatin - i.e., statin depletion of isoprenoids impairs Rho-family prenylation, producing secondary actin/tubulin texture, rounding and shrinkage at high micromolar doses that the atlas reads as Actin disruptors. PMID 31687098 and PMID 15571475 similarly discuss lovastatin/statin as cholesterol-lowering agents via HMG-CoA reductase, not direct cytoskeleton targets.

Lesson: With a limited atlas, simultaneous actin+ tubulin surge + cell loss should trigger suspicion of off-target/downstream cytoskeletal effect rather than direct Actin disruptor, and requires onset-dose titration and orthogonal biochemical assays (actin polymerization vs tubulin polymerization, and Rho prenylation readouts) before assigning p>0.6.

What was right:
- Extreme high-dose morphology real (e2,e4) with tub_glcm_contrast up to +66.8, actin contrast +41.7, dose rho 0.8-1.0
- Baseline at 0.15-0.5uM e3,e5 vs saturated at 5uM e2 confirmed steep threshold requiring onset dose
- Review correctly identified atlas margin 4/10 vs 3/10 e6 insufficient and 0.62 premature

What was wrong or missed:
- Mapped Cholesterol-lowering downstream cytoskeletal effect to direct Actin disruptor due to atlas lacking cholesterol class
- Weighted NSC 2/4 and k-neighbour 4/10 over microscopist Microtubule stabilizer call e10
- Used n=4 rho p=0.2 e7,e8 as supportive trend and submitted without requested 1.5uM well

Proposed next experiment: Acquire 1.5uM onset well plus full 0.5-5uM titration with act_* vs tub_* texture and act_tub_ratio trajectory + blinded reference actin and microtubule compounds; add orthogonal assays: in vitro actin polymerization/F-actin sedimentation vs tubulin polymerization counter-assay and Rho geranylgeranylation/prenylation readout to separate HMG-CoA reductase downstream cytoskeleton effect from direct actin disruption.
